chapter: Early life and the New Orleans band scene
title: Born on Conti Street, raised in the Fifth Ward, working the district
summary: He was born on Conti, raised in the Fifth Ward among Black musicians, and describes small-band pay and nightly work in the Storyville district.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was wondering, which part of the town were you raised in? Where were you born?

I was born right here on Conti, between Dauphin and Bourbon, right where Bruce Oswald's Restore. Right there? Yes, right in the backyard I was born. Were you raised in there? I was raised all the way, I was left there in 1900. And my father went in the business on Orleans and Billory and I was around the Fifth Ward all my life. Raised in the Fifth Ward. And I was raised around a lot of colored musicians. I mean the way all the colored musicians lived in the Fifth Ward, most of them. Most of them. Every one of them. And they all just had, you know, a talent. You know what I mean? They had bands running around, taking jobs and everything. While you, many of the times we would take a job. Four men. Six dollars. Down and a half a piece. Guitar, bass, clarinet, and trumpet. And there was a big winning there, baby. From the old district. When they start putting white men in the old tenderloin district. That's the full voice for those walls. So that's why we all went there. And of course, we got a down and a half a night. We were working nine o'clock at night. We worked about four or five o'clock in the morning. As long as they're doing business, we stay there. We get paid every night. What? We were making eight, ten, twelve dollars a night, too. We're making eight, ten. So. Our salary was only a dollar and a half at night. Get all the cigarettes, all the drinks, all the eats, you know. You don't even worry about it.
